title: Brother Lustig variant
summary: Brother Lustig was a merry discharged soldier who possessed nothing in the world except four kreuzers and a knapsack, yet he sang cheerful songs wherever he walked....
full_text:
Brother Lustig was a merry discharged soldier who possessed nothing in the world except four kreuzers and a knapsack, yet he sang cheerful songs wherever he walked.

Along the road, he met Saint Peter disguised as a poor beggar. Lustig shared his last coins and bread with cheerful generosity. In gratitude, Saint Peter granted him a magical knapsack: whatever Lustig commanded to enter the knapsack was bound to jump inside immediately!

When Lustig stopped at an inn, he ordered roasted geese from the air into his knapsack and dined like a king. Later, he arrived at a haunted castle where terrifying demons tormented the region. Lustig stepped inside, waited until the demons attempted to tear him apart, and shouted: "Into the knapsack, all of you!"

The howling demons tumbled into the sack. Lustig carried the heavy knapsack to the village blacksmith, laid it upon the anvil, and had the smith hammer it with his heaviest sledgehammer until the demons screamed for mercy and swore never to torment mortal souls again!

When his life's journey ended, Lustig marched up to the pearly gates. Saint Peter hesitated to admit the rowdy wanderer, but Lustig tossed his knapsack over the golden threshold and shouted, "I wish myself inside my knapsack!" Instantly, he found himself inside heaven, laughing heartily and greeting the angels with cheerful comradeship.
moral: A merry heart and unshakeable good cheer overcome all trials and turn every obstacle into joy.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Brother Lustig variant"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
